text: Stars Dance is the debut solo album by American singer Selena Gomez, released on July 19, 2013, by Hollywood Records. Gomez began planning the project in 2012, announcing that her band Selena Gomez & the Scene would take an indefinite hiatus. The album is an EDM and electropop record that incorporates elements of dubstep, techno, disco, electro house, and worldbeat. She worked on the album through March 2013 with producers including Rock Mafia and the Cataracs. Upon release, Stars Dance received generally mixed reviews, with critics praising Gomez's maturing image and vocal and lyrical content, while criticizing its electronic-heavy production. The album debuted at number 1 on the Billboard 200, selling 97,000 copies domestically in its first week, a figure later surpassed by her 2015 album Revival, which sold 117,000 units in its first week. Stars Dance became her fourth Top 20 entry in the United Kingdom, peaking at number 14, and topped the charts in Canada, Norway, Mexico, Taiwan, and China. By 2017, it had sold an estimated 410,000 copies in the United States. The lead single, "Come & Get It," featured heavy electronic and worldbeat themes and became Gomez's first Top 10 entry in the United States, entering the Top 10 in the United Kingdom, Ireland, and Canada, and reached number 2 on the Mainstream Top 40 chart. "Slow Down" reached the Top 30 in the United States and also reached the Top 10 of the Mainstream Top 40. Gomez promoted the album through high-profile performances, including the 2013 Billboard Music Awards, and embarked on the Stars Dance Tour (2013). Selena Gomez & the Scene's third studio album, When the Sun Goes Down (2011), was musically rooted in electropop and dance-pop, similar to their second album, A Year Without Rain (2010). Although reviews for that album were mixed, it was a commercial success. In January 2012, Gomez announced a musical hiatus to focus on acting, stating the band would go their separate ways. Despite this, she confirmed in October 2012 that work had begun on an upcoming solo album, which she later described as her debut. She announced the lead single would be released the following month and the album would follow in the summer. On April 15, she revealed plans for her first world tour, the Stars Dance Tour. On June 3, she officially confirmed the album's title, Stars Dance, and revealed the track listing and cover art. On her return to music, Gomez stated she wanted to write about personal experiences and tell a story, as she had not had time before. For the album, she worked with The Cataracs, Stargate, and Rock Mafia, with Rock Mafia having previously worked on singles with The Scene. She emphasized greater creative control, stating it was the hardest record she had ever worked on. Jason Evigan noted that Gomez had grown into a respected electronic pop dance artist. Prior to the album's release, Gomez announced she would take a musical hiatus after Stars Dance, citing her love for acting and film. Following the album's announcement, rumors spread that most of the album was about her relationship with Justin Bieber. After the release of "Come & Get It," these rumors intensified, and Gomez confirmed the song was not about Bieber, though she later stated that "Love Will Remember" is about her relationship with Bieber, citing an early leaked version with a voicemail from Bieber that was removed. She called "Love Will Remember" the most personal track on the record and said it was a sweet way to release it. "Birthday" was the first song recorded for the album. Gomez listed "Forget Forever" as one of her favorite tracks, describing it as a beautiful song with emotional meaning and a special studio experience, and noted it was about forgetting past troubles. She later said it was about enjoying the present. Recording artist Jennifer Lopez wanted to record "Save the Day" for her 2013 album but failed to secure it from Gomez. "Come & Get It" was initially recorded by Rihanna for her 2011 album Talk That Talk, but she decided not to use it. Musically, Stars Dance is rooted in EDM and pop, specifically electropop, with strong elements of dubstep, techno, disco, and worldbeat. Jocelyn Vena of MTV News described it as "dance-song-heavy" dubstep with wobbly synths, loopy vocals, fist-pumping beats, and crunchy breakdowns. Caroline Sullivan of The Guardian noted its efficient movement from EDM to Bollywood. Most tracks feature dubstep breakdowns, synth stabs, and according to Jim Farber of the New York Daily News, a frisson of sex previously absent from her work. Jason Evigan noted ethnic influences, such as tribal dance drums, similar to Jennifer Lopez's music. August Brown of the Los Angeles Times called it a "sassy" pop-EDM album with "oxygen-sucking" sub-bass and trap snares, noting Spring Breakers' influence. He described it as a blend of pop sugar from the Disney era with broken glass and club bathroom nosebleeds. The title track "Stars Dance" is described as "kind of sensual" and features an orchestral-dubstep beat. "Like a Champion" includes Jamaican and reggae influences and features Gomez singing in a Bajan accent, drawing comparisons to Rihanna. "Save the Day" is about moments when one doesn't want a moment to end, and is described as a "thumping" Latin pop and house song. "Write Your Name" is about falling in love and features a rap verse by Gomez and dubstep elements. "B.E.A.T." is a "sexy" urban hip-hop song with minimal spoken word electro, described as "infectious and definitely racier than usual." Gomez cited Britney Spears, Janet Jackson, Skrillex, Taylor Swift, and Christina Aguilera as major influences. She noted Skrillex inspired her with baby dubstep, having previously worked on the Spring Breakers soundtrack. In an interview with Teen Vogue, she mentioned Ellie Goulding, describing the record as "a little Ellie Goulding-ish, a little island-y feel." The album opens with "Birthday," an electropunk song with sparse drums, trap snares, and vocal chants, described as a "candy-coated, clap-happy club anthem" with girl power and sex appeal. "Slow Down" is a high-octane, uptempo dance-pop and EDM song with a dubstep chorus, funk guitars, a four-on-the-floor beat, and a spoken word outro, lyrically speaking of slowing down a relationship. "Stars Dance" is a "breathy and sultry" dubstep song with an orchestral-dubstep beat, with Gomez's soft voice taking center stage over sexy synth-beats and wallowing melodies. "Like a Champion" is a dancehall song with funk, reggae, and soca influences. "Come & Get It" is a tribal electropop and popstep song with a Bhangra beat, sonic drops, and Indian music influences, lyrically about a female lover rekindling a past romance. "Forget Forever" is a dance-pop and synthpop song with an EDM beat and house music breakdowns, lyrically about a breakup. Sam Lansky of Idolator called it an "electrifying dance-pop banger" with a strong chorus and anthemic beat, while Nate Jones of Popdust called it "bright and expansive" with vocals flying over an EDM beat. "Save the Day" is a "thumping" Latin pop and house song. "B.E.A.T." is described as "minimal spoken word electro" and "infectious and definitely racier than usual." "Write Your Name" is an "exotic" electronic dance and house music song with a rap verse and dubstep elements. "Forget Forever" and "Write Your Name" both avoid the bombast of typical Guetta-style tracks. Gomez promoted the album through interviews and televised performances, including On Air with Ryan Seacrest on April 8, 2013, her first televised performance of "Come & Get It" at the 2013 MTV Movie Awards on April 14, a performance on Dancing with the Stars on April 16, a performance on The Ellen Degeneres Show on April 18, a performance on The Late Show with David Letterman on April 25, and at the 2013 Radio Disney Music Awards on April 27. She performed "Come & Get It" again at the 2013 Billboard Music Awards on May 19 and on The Graham Norton Show days later. She performed "Slow Down" for the first time at MuchMusic Headquarters on May 30 and performed both "Come & Get It" and "Slow Down" at the Macy's 4th of July Fireworks Spectacular on July 4. She performed "Come & Get It" on This Morning in the United Kingdom and on Good Morning America to coincide with the album's release, and on Live! With Kelly and Michael in September. Following the release of "Slow Down," she performed it on The View and The Late Show with David Letterman, and on The X Factor in the United States. She was selected as the halftime performer for the Dallas Cowboys vs. Oakland Raiders Thanksgiving game, performing a medley of "Like a Champion," "Slow Down," and "Come & Get It." The Stars Dance Tour (2013) promoted the album and visited the United States and Asia, earning over $36 million at the box office, though dates in Australia and Japan were canceled due to personal issues. "Come & Get It" was released as the lead single on April 7, 2013, and by July 2013 had become one of Gomez's most successful singles, peaking at number 6 on the US Billboard Hot 100 and the Canadian Hot 100, and was certified 3× Platinum by the RIAA. The music video premiered on MTV on May 7, 2013.

Selena Gomez was selected to perform as the halftime act during the Dallas Cowboys vs. Oakland Raiders game on Thanksgiving, where she performed a medley of "Like a Champion," "Slow Down," and "Come & Get It." The Stars Dance Tour (2013), which was originally scheduled to include dates in Australia and Japan, was cancelled due to personal issues and instead promoted the tour through performances in the United States and Asia, earning over $36 million at the box office. "Come & Get It" was released as the lead single on April 7, 2013, and by July 2013 had reached number 6 on both the US Billboard Hot 100 and the Canadian Hot 100, earning 3× Platinum certification from the RIAA; its music video premiered on MTV on May 7, 2013, directed by Anthony Mandler. "Slow Down" was released as a promotional single on June 3, 2013, via instant digital download with the pre-order of the album on iTunes, co-produced by The Cataracs and David Kuncio, and later released as the official second single on August 13, 2013, peaking at number 27 on the Billboard Hot 100; its official video was uploaded to YouTube on July 19, 2013. Stars Dance received mixed reviews; critics praised the album's production, lyrics, and Gomez's vocals, but criticized her lack of a distinct musical identity, often comparing her to Rihanna. At Metacritic, the album received an average score of 59, indicating "mixed or average reviews." Tim Sendra from AllMusic awarded it three-and-a-half stars, highlighting "Slow Down," "Save the Day," and "Undercover" as highlights and calling it another strong entry in her catalog. Stephen Unwin from Express.co.uk compared it to Vanessa Hudgens, noting the album's shift to more adult themes. Two Guardian reviews were issued: Kitty Empire awarded three stars, while Hermione Hoby gave two stars, criticizing Gomez for lacking a strong hit-making ability and comparing the work to Rihanna. August Brown from the Los Angeles Times described the album as blending pop sugar from her Disney era with "broken glass and a club bathroom nosebleed," rooted in today's pop-EDM trends. Natalie Palmer from Entertainmentwise praised the album for attempting something new, noting it diverged from bubblegum pop or angry rock, opting for an edgier sound. Matthew Horton from Virgin Media gave two stars, criticizing the lack of personality and vocal strength, calling the album "identikit" and unoriginal. Simon Price from The Independent awarded one star, stating there was no standout track to redeem the record. Ron Harris from The Huffington Post felt the album failed to meet expectations, saying Gomez "punched the clock" and worked through a pre-written musical plot, and noted it had less personality than her earlier work with The Scene. Stars Dance debuted at number one on the Billboard 200, selling 97,000 copies in its first week—Gomez's first number one and highest first-week sales until surpassed by Revival, which sold 117,000 copies in its first week. The album fell to number eight in its second week (selling 31,000 copies, a 68% drop), then to number thirteen, number eighteen, and number twenty-five in its fifth week, rising to number twenty-four after a 23% sales increase (selling 17,213 copies) and reaching number twenty-one, before dropping to number thirty-three the following week (selling just over 7,000 copies). The album spent a total of twenty-five weeks on the Billboard 200, with its last appearance on the week ending January 25, 2014. It debuted at number one on the Canadian Albums Chart with 16,500 copies sold in its first week—her first number one in Canada and surpassing her previous album's first-week sales by over 5,000. On August 27, 2013, it received a Gold certification from the CRIA for sales exceeding 40,000. It entered the top five at number five on the New Zealand Albums Chart. In the UK, it debuted and peaked at number fourteen, spending four weeks on the chart; in Ireland, it peaked at number nine and spent six weeks; in Australia, it peaked at number eight. The album was more successful internationally: it debuted at number one in Mexico, was certified Gold for 30,000 sales, reached number two in Portugal (certified Platinum), peaked at number eight in Brazil (certified Platinum), and reached number eight in Australia. Credits are adapted from the album's liner notes. Sampling credits and shipment/sales figures are based on certification alone.
